reference.source: TradingView Help Center, On Balance Volume (OBV)
reference.quote: The On Balance Volume indicator (OBV) is used in technical analysis to measure buying and selling pressure.

draw.today: 11 'obv' labels (x 192.2-1026.1, y 77.4-417.2) at price while the OBV pane is drawn below. The pane draws only the line -- obv_pane has no segments or markers (indicator_series.rs:392-409) -- so the concept's actual mark, a price/OBV divergence, exists nowhere except as a word at price. A cumulative volume line has no price level, so the label's height is meaningless as well as duplicated.
draw.canonical: one cumulative OBV line in its own pane, auto-scaled -- 'used ... to measure buying and selling pressure' -- with the divergence, when drawn, as a segment on the OBV line, not a word at price.

fires.our_rule: OBV is defined on every bar; price/OBV divergences are emitted when the tail confirms them (indicator_signals.rs:26 via oscillator_divergence at 630, n >= 40)
fires.their_rule: TradingView plots OBV continuously in its own pane and marks no divergence; the divergence line is drawn on the OBV trace

rule_as_data.rule: obv = cumsum(sign(close - prev_close) * volume) => divergence when price and obv disagree at two confirmed pivots

warmup.before: OBV exists from bar 2; the divergence detector requires n >= 40

reference.quote: The Accumulation Distribution (ADL) indicator is a cumulative volume-based technical analysis tool that measures the flow of money into and out of a security.

draw.today: 20 'ad line' labels (x 155.8-1045.4, y 77.4-416.6) at price while the A/D pane is drawn below. The pane draws the line only (ad_pane has no marks, indicator_series.rs:644-657), so the divergence the event names is drawn nowhere but as a word at price -- and the A/D line is not a price.
draw.canonical: one cumulative A/D line in its own pane, auto-scaled -- 'a cumulative volume-based technical analysis tool that measures the flow of money into and out of a security'.

fires.our_rule: A/D is defined on every bar; price/A-D divergences are emitted when the tail confirms them (indicator_signals.rs:30 via oscillator_divergence at 630, n >= 40)
fires.their_rule: TradingView plots the A/D line continuously in its own pane and marks no divergence; the divergence is drawn on the line

rule_as_data.rule: ad = cumsum(((close - low) - (high - close)) / (high - low) * volume) => divergence when price and ad disagree at two confirmed pivots

warmup.before: A/D exists from bar 2; the divergence detector requires n >= 40

reference.source: TradingView Help Center, Chaikin Money Flow (CMF)
reference.quote: Chaikin Money Flow (CMF) is a technical analysis indicator used to measure Money Flow Volume over a set period of time.

draw.today: 50 'cmf' labels (x 280.1-1081.9, y 80.2-447.3) at price while the CMF pane with its zero line is drawn below. A ratio bounded in -1..1 is being drawn as a price word.
draw.canonical: one CMF line in its own pane, zero line, auto-scaled -- 'a technical analysis indicator used to measure Money Flow Volume over a set period of time'.

fires.our_rule: CMF(20) is defined on every bar; a label is emitted when it crosses zero (indicator_signals.rs:52-55, n > 22)
fires.their_rule: TradingView plots CMF continuously across zero and marks no cross; the line crossing zero is the reading

rule_as_data.rule: cmf = sum(mfv, 20) / sum(volume, 20) => signal when cmf crosses zero

warmup.before: CMF(20) exists from bar 20; the detector requires n > 22

reference.source: TradingView Help Center, Money Flow Index (MFI)
reference.quote: The Money Flow Index indicator (MFI) is a tool used in technical analysis for measuring buying and selling pressure.

draw.today: 17 'mfi' labels (x 130-998.3, y 70.4-486.1) at price while the MFI pane -- fixed 0-100, 80/20 -- is drawn below. The bounded oscillator is already the drawing; the labels add a price-space copy.
draw.canonical: one MFI line in its own pane, fixed 0-100, levels at 80 and 20 -- 'a tool used ... for measuring buying and selling pressure', with no mark at price.

fires.our_rule: MFI(14) is defined on every bar; a label is emitted when it enters the 80/20 zone (indicator_signals.rs:65-67, n > 16)
fires.their_rule: TradingView plots MFI continuously against 80/20 and marks no zone entry; the line entering the band is the reading

rule_as_data.rule: mfi = MFI(typical, volume, 14) => signal when mfi enters 80/20

warmup.before: MFI(14) exists from bar 14; the detector requires n > 16

reference.source: TradingView Help Center, Anchored VWAP drawing tool
reference.quote: Anchored VWAP displays the volume-weighted average price for a specific time period, starting from a user-selected point.

draw.today: 50 'anchored vwap' labels (x 417.3-1081.9, y 46.8-479.7) at price while two anchored VWAP lines are drawn on the same price frame. Here the label's scale is at least a price, but it is still a second mark over a line that already shows the level.
draw.canonical: one VWAP line per anchor on the price plot, running from the anchor bar forward -- 'starting from a user-selected point' -- with no word at price.

fires.our_rule: two AVWAP lines (newest swing high and newest swing low) are defined on every bar; a label is emitted when price crosses either anchor line (indicator_signals.rs:91-93, n > 30)
fires.their_rule: TradingView draws the anchored VWAP continuously from its anchor and marks no cross; the line crossing price is the reading

rule_as_data.rule: avwap(anchor) = cumsum(typical * volume from anchor) / cumsum(volume from anchor) => signal when close crosses either anchor line

warmup.before: a 3-bar fractal anchor exists after ~7 bars; the detector requires n > 30
